description.p: Muga is a GTK 4 and libadwaita photo gallery for Linux desktops and phones. It indexes local media folders, shows cached thumbnails, plays videos, edits photos, connects to Nextcloud Photos, and includes a camera for photo and video capture.
On Halium and gst-droid based phones such as FuriOS devices, Muga can use the device camera HAL directly for flash, video light, orientation, and geotagging workflows.
Fixes: paging through photos follows the picture when the screen is rotated. Holding the phone sideways used to turn the pages with an up and down swipe; left and right works again.
Packaging: the translations are compiled during the install, and the desktop entry starts the installed launcher.

Reliability: rotating or moving a photo can no longer damage or overwrite it, a hand-edited settings file or a damaged media index no longer stops the app from starting, and an interrupted update rolls itself back.

Fixes: cameras reporting a resolution range (libcamera) are found again, large libraries no longer load in full before the first frame, oversized images are refused before they exhaust memory, and rotated controls are laid out correctly.

Performance: off-thread thumbnail and image decoding, smoother scrolling and swiping, faster re-scans (unchanged files are skipped), EXIF search via the full-text index, and lighter settings/sync work.
